scenes.voiceover_script: The core driver was geographical divergence. In Western Europe, heavy defensive armor and formation ceiling were vital for daylight raids. In the Pacific, sheer nautical range was the non-negotiable metric. To gain 600 miles of range, engineers had to accept thinner high-aspect wings, fundamentally altering handling characteristics.

scenes.voiceover_script: Beyond flight performance, wartime procurement was dictated by industrial throughput. Rather than an arbitrary rivalry, Why Did the SR-71 Blackbird Leak Fuel on the Runway? was an intentional doctrine matching specific aircraft to distinct geographic and industrial constraints. Automotive stamping techniques permitted rapid airframe production at volumes that traditional aviation tooling could not match. Tactical planners recognized that operational availability in numbers often superseded marginal flight-handling preferences.
